logline: In an alternate Edo Japan occupied by aliens, a lazy, silver-haired samurai and his misfit crew take on odd jobs while somehow stumbling into the most consequential battles in history - all while relentlessly breaking the fourth wall.

renewal.note: The anime adaptation concluded with Gintama: The Final film in 2021, adapting the manga's ending arc. The main series ran 367 TV episodes across four seasons from 2006 to 2018.

bollymeter.basis: MAL score of 8.3 across a substantial viewer base; the foundational run that established Gintama's reputation as anime's defining comedy-action hybrid with genuine emotional range.

pull_quotes.text: Gintama has always been earnestly self-aware, irreverent without being cynical.

seasons.review_body: Gintama ran on TV Tokyo from April 2006 to March 2010, produced by Sunrise, across 201 episodes. The series spent its first two cours building a reputation for parody - Gin-san breaks the fourth wall, references other anime, and treats absurdism as its default mode. Then it periodically drops the comedy entirely for serious multi-episode arcs (the Benizakura Arc, the Yoshiwara arc) that land with full dramatic weight precisely because the comedy has disarmed the viewer's defences. Anime News Network's Carlo Santos called it a one-of-a-kind comedy with a characters' depth and gag density rare in any serialised format. The sheer length deterred casual entry but rewarded investment.

episode_reviews.title: The Strongest Army in the Universe Has Arrived at Jump Festa!!
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The episode that became the definitive example of Gintama's fourth-wall comedic mode: a Jump Festa event episode where the cast abandons all pretence of fiction and addresses the audience directly. Beloved by long-time fans as the purest expression of Gintoki's worldview - nothing is sacred, least of all the show itself.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Gintoki's direct address to the viewer mid-crisis - the show's fundamental contract made explicit.

episode_reviews.title: Even if You're Disrespected, Don't Disrespect
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The Benizakura Arc finale: the tonal pivot that told the entire anime community Gintama was more than a parody machine. After 60 episodes of jokes about episode budgets, the series delivered a sword fight with genuine emotional stakes and production values that silenced anyone who dismissed it as a comedy.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Gintoki's final clash in the Benizakura arc - the moment the franchise proved it earned its emotional weight.

bollymeter.basis: MAL scores climbed through Gintama' as the dramatic arcs - particularly the Shogun Assassination Arc groundwork - began to match the comedy's reputation.

seasons.review_body: Gintama' (with the apostrophe indicating a relaunch rather than a true sequel) aired April 2011 to March 2012 across 51 episodes. The series returned after a year's gap with a sharper editorial sense, tightening the ratio of gag episodes to serious arcs. The Yoshiwara in Flames Arc and the Four Devas Arc belong to this run and represent the franchise's best balance of comedy and consequence. MAL community scores rose to the high 8s, tracking an audience that had cleared the early-entry hump and was now rewarded with material that justified the investment. A 13-episode continuation, Gintama' Enchousen, aired October 2012 to March 2013.
seasons.season_over_season: Tighter pacing and a higher ratio of consequential arcs make Gintama' the point where casual watchers become franchise advocates.

bollymeter.basis: Gintama degrees (MAL 9.05, ranked #72 globally) is the franchise's critical and community peak - the Shogun Assassination and Farewell Shinsengumi arcs are considered among anime's finest dramatic storytelling.

seasons.review_body: Gintama degrees aired April 2015 to March 2016 - 51 episodes that constitute the franchise's acknowledged masterwork. The MAL community score of 9.05 places it among anime's all-time highest-rated seasons, ranked in the global top 100. The Shogun Assassination Arc and Farewell Shinsengumi Arc deliver tragic, consequential drama at a scale the comedy had only gestured toward before, with character deaths and political stakes that recontextualise the entire franchise. Sunrise's animation reached its highest production quality on the series here. Critics noted that Gintama had achieved something genuinely rare: a long-running comedy that could make the audience cry without it feeling manipulative.
seasons.season_over_season: The franchise's defining achievement - years of comedy investment pay off as emotional stakes reach their highest and the production quality matches them.

episode_reviews.title: The Shogun's Last Stand
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The episode that defines what Gintama's decade of comedy was building toward. The Shogun's protection arc concludes here - and the writing earns every emotional note precisely because the series spent years making viewers care about this man through jokes and small moments rather than heroic staging.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The Shogun's final moments: Gintama's central thesis - that even buffoons protect something worth protecting - delivered at full dramatic weight.

bollymeter.basis: The Silver Soul Arc brought the main narrative to its conclusion across 2017-2018 with the emotional and thematic payoffs the entire franchise had been building; MAL scores remained in the high 8s through the finale.

seasons.review_body: Gintama: The Silver Soul Arc aired January 2017 to October 2018 across 51 episodes, delivering the adaptation of Hideaki Sorachi's manga endgame. The arc gathered every major character and faction into a final conflict, rewarding viewers who had followed the franchise through more than a decade of gags and tears. IMDb's overall series score of 8.7 reflects the franchise's standing across its entire run. The Silver Soul Arc is at once a proper conclusion and a farewell - the comedy dropped almost entirely in the final stretch as the series committed fully to its dramatic register. The Gintama: The Final film in 2021 completed the adaptation.
seasons.season_over_season: The franchise's endgame - narrative threads from all prior seasons converge in a conclusion that justifies Gintama's unusual scale and patience.
